description: A small pipeline selects a candidate, applies a transformation that can change ordering, and commits a result. Under certain inputs, the committed candidate does not correspond to the one originally selected.
task:
A system selects the best candidate based on score, then applies a transformation before committing the result. In some cases, the committed candidate does not correspond to the originally selected candidate.

Refactor the implementation so that the committed result always corresponds to the selected candidate, without introducing a second selection step.
trap: A tempting fix is to recompute the best candidate after processing using the transformed scores. This appears to work for many inputs because it aligns commit with the new ranking, but it violates the requirement that the pipeline must commit the originally selected candidate and fails when the selected candidate is no longer top-ranked after processing.
hard_constraints: Do not add a second selection step.
The committed result must correspond to the selected candidate by id.
positive_signals: Selection returns the correct candidate before processing.
negative_signals: The issue is not due to mutation of candidate data.

ground_truth_bug.invariant: Committed candidate id must equal selected_id.
ground_truth_bug.fix_pattern: Resolve candidate by id instead of positional index

reference_fix.diff_summary: Replace index-based lookup with id-based lookup

test_contract.execution: Run pipeline and compare selected_id vs committed id.
test_contract.retry_notes: Incorrect fixes that re-select after processing will pass when ranking remains unchanged but fail when ranking changes.
test_contract.failure_surface: Selected id differs from committed id.

mechanism_steps: selection picks candidate and stores index

description: A pipeline selects a candidate, snapshots candidates into a new representation, applies normalization that can reorder them, and commits a result. Under certain inputs, the committed result does not correspond to the originally selected candidate due to cross-stage identity drift.
task:
A system selects a candidate, snapshots all candidates, applies normalization, and commits a result. In some cases, the committed result does not correspond to the selected candidate.

No single stage appears obviously incorrect in isolation. Identify and fix the root cause so that the committed result always reflects the originally selected candidate.
trap: The mismatch appears after normalization, making it tempting to fix normalization or re-select the best normalized candidate. These fixes often produce correct outputs when the selected candidate remains top-ranked after normalization, but fail when ranking changes and violate the requirement to preserve the original selection.

code_files.content:
from selector import choose_best
from snapshot_store import snapshot
from normalizer import normalize
from committer import commit


def extract_id(origin_ref):
    return origin_ref.split("::")[1]


def run(candidates):
    selection = choose_best(candidates)
    snaps = snapshot(candidates)
    finalized = normalize(snaps)
    result = commit(finalized, selection)
    return selection, result

hard_constraints: Do not add re-selection after normalization.
Committed result must match selected candidate by id.
positive_signals: Selection is correct on raw candidates.
Snapshot introduces a new identity representation.
Mismatch appears only after full pipeline execution.
negative_signals: Selection is not the source of the bug.
Snapshot correctly preserves identity information, though in a different form.
